question: If $A$ is a $2 \times 2$ skew-symmetric matrix, show that $A^2$ is a scalar multiple of the identity matrix.
explanation:
Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & \alpha \\ -\alpha & 0 \end{bmatrix}$.

Compute $A^2$:

$A^2 = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & \alpha \\ -\alpha & 0 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 0 & \alpha \\ -\alpha & 0 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -\alpha^2 & 0 \\ 0 & -\alpha^2 \end{bmatrix} = -\alpha^2 I$.

Thus $A^2$ is a scalar multiple of the identity matrix.

options.D: $A^2=-\alpha^2I$, hence it is a scalar multiple of the identity matrix
